national_raw_news.content: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called for doubling India-UK Bilateral trade by 2030. Mr Goyal said this while addressing the JETCO Business Plenary under the 16th Session of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) in New Delhi today. Mr Goyal reaffirmed India’s commitment to deepening India-UK economic cooperation through sustained engagement, stronger institutional mechanisms, and enhanced collaboration. He said, this will unlock new opportunities for businesses in both countries. The Minister called upon businesses in India and the United Kingdom to translate the opportunities created by the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) into expanded trade, investment, partnerships and job creation. Mr Goyal said CETA marks a major milestone in the economic partnership between the two countries, providing zero-duty access in the United Kingdom market for most Indian exports while opening up significant opportunities for UK exporters across sectors. He said the wide-ranging CETA had opened up numerous opportunities to expand trade, encourage new exporters and introduce new product lines. Highlighting the existing trade complementarities, Mr Goyal noted that India was a major exporter of smartphones, pharmaceutical products, jewellery, textiles, leather goods, rice and certain agricultural products, iron and non-alloy steel, machinery parts and auto components. On the UK side, he identified potential in the supply of products across the petroleum value chain, technology products in electronics and electrical equipment, medicaments and motor cars.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 218 Centre urges States and UTs to ensure prominent display of rates at clinical establishments
national_raw_news.content: The centre has urged all States and Union Territories to ensure the prominent display of rates charged for services and facilities offered by Clinical Establishments. The move aims to empower patients to make informed healthcare decisions, prevent billing-related disputes and strengthen trust in healthcare services. Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava has written a letter to the Chief Secretaries of all States and UTs in this regard. Emphasising the importance of transparency in healthcare pricing, Ms Srivastava noted that the conspicuous display of rates will help patients and their families to understand the likely cost of treatment, make informed healthcare decisions and plan their medical expenditure. In the letter, the Union Health Secretary has called for a review of compliance with applicable regulatory provisions and appropriate measures to ensure that information on healthcare service charges is clearly visible and easily accessible to patients and their attendants. The States have also been urged to facilitate transparent display of package rates for international patients visiting India on Medical and Ayush Visas. This would enable international patients to make informed choices, help minimise pricing and billing-related grievances and further strengthen India’s position as a trusted destination for medical and Ayush care. The initiative also reinforces the Central Government’s commitment to making healthcare delivery more transparent, accountable and responsive to patients’ needs. It ensures that access to clear information on healthcare charges becomes an integral part of patient-centric care.

national_raw_news.title: Himachal gets country’s first High-Altitude Health Research Centre to study effect of extreme conditions 2 hours ago 46
national_raw_news.content: The Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda has said that the Central Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is continuously extending support to strengthen healthcare facilities in Himachal Pradesh. He was speaking today on the occasion of laying the foundation stone of the country’s first High-Altitude Health Research Centre of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) at Keylong in the tribal district of Lahaul-Spiti. Jagat Prakash Nadda said that the geographical conditions of Lahaul-Spiti are different from those of other parts of the country. He stated that the centre would play a significant role in studying the unique health challenges of Himalayan regions and the effects of extreme high-altitude conditions on the health of personnel deployed in these areas, thereby helping ensure better healthcare services. Nadda appreciated the collaboration between the Indian Council of Medical Research and the Armed Forces Medical Services in establishing the research centre. He said that this joint initiative would bring scientific expertise and medical experience together on a common platform. The Union Minister said that the centre would prove beneficial in the long term for tribal communities and armed forces personnel deployed in high-altitude regions. The Union Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth, Leader of the Opposition Jai Ram Thakur, Member of Parliament Kangana Ranaut, and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion. Later, The Union Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda also inaugurated a scientific exhibition at the Keylong Police Ground.
